question: What is the main job of diuretic drugs in the body?

options.A: Stimulate the filtration rate within the renal glomerulus
options.B: Decrease the total amount of blood filtered daily
options.C: Increase urine volume by stopping sodium reabsorption
options.D: Promote the retention of essential plasma electrolytes

explanation: Diuretics block sodium from being reabsorbed in the kidneys, which makes water stay in the tubules and increases urine output. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h1)

question: Why does blocking sodium reabsorption cause the body to get rid of more water?

options.A: Water naturally follows sodium down osmotic gradients
options.B: Filtered water is created rapidly by the diuretic drug
options.C: Renal tubules actively pump water out when sodium drops
options.D: Sodium destruction triggers a local release of body fluids

explanation: Through osmosis, water moves toward areas with a higher concentration of solutes, so staying sodium pulls water along into the urine. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h1)

question: Which group of diuretics works on the loop of Henle to produce the strongest fluid loss?
explanation: Loop diuretics act on the thick ascending limb of the loop of Henle, leading to a large amount of fluid and electrolyte loss. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h2)

question: Where in the nephron do thiazide diuretics mainly work?
explanation: Thiazide medications target and block sodium and chloride reabsorption right at the early part of the distal convoluted tubule. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h2)

question: Which medication is the standard example of a loop diuretic?
explanation: Furosemide is the most commonly prescribed loop diuretic and serves as the main drug of choice for this class. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h3)

question: Giving a loop diuretic too fast through an intravenous line puts the patient at risk for which problem?

options.B: Total loss of gastric acid secretion

explanation: A rapid IV push of a loop diuretic can lead to ototoxicity, which causes ringing in the ears or hearing issues. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h3)

question: Thiazide diuretics are most commonly used as a first-line treatment for which condition?
explanation: Thiazide diuretics help lower chronic high blood pressure steadily over time, making them a top choice for hypertension. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h4)

question: How do thiazides handle calcium differently than loop diuretics?

options.A: Thiazides promote calcium reabsorption while loop diuretics increase calcium excretion
options.B: Neither drug class has any direct or indirect effect on renal calcium transport
options.C: Both drug classes completely stop all forms of calcium processing in the nephron
options.D: Thiazides excrete large amounts of calcium while loop diuretics retain all serum calcium

explanation: Thiazides help the body hold onto calcium, whereas loop diuretics cause calcium to be lost in the urine. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h4)

question: What is the main electrolyte imbalance linked to potassium-sparing diuretics?
explanation: Because these drugs prevent potassium from leaving the body, they can cause potassium levels in the blood to climb too high. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h5)

question: How does spironolactone manage to hold onto potassium while causing diuresis?

options.A: By blocking aldosterone receptors in the late distal nephron
options.B: By destroying carbonic anhydrase enzymes in the proximal tubule
options.C: By stimulating the active reabsorption of sodium ions in the glomerulus
options.D: By increasing osmotic pressure inside the descending loop of Henle

explanation: Spironolactone blocks the action of aldosterone, which stops sodium from being kept and stops potassium from being lost. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h5)

question: What is the main reason a nurse would give intravenous mannitol?
explanation: Mannitol draws water out of brain tissue into the bloodstream through osmosis, which quickly lowers pressure inside the skull. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h6)

question: What happens in the body when acetazolamide blocks carbonic anhydrase in the proximal tubule?

options.A: Glucose is completely reabsorbed from the renal filtrate
options.B: Bicarbonate is excreted, leading to metabolic acidosis
options.C: Sodium is heavily retained, causing rapid fluid overload
options.D: Potassium levels rise significantly across all body tissues

explanation: Blocking this enzyme stops bicarbonate from being reabsorbed, so it leaves in the urine and can cause a mild acidic state in the blood. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h6)

question: What is the most reliable way to track daily fluid changes in a patient taking a diuretic?
explanation: Weighing the patient at the same time every day reveals sudden fluid retention or water loss faster than almost any other check. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h7)

question: Why must the nurse watch a patient's blood pressure closely after starting a diuretic?

options.A: Sudden fluid shifts cause an immediate spike in systemic pressure
options.B: Vasoconstriction always follows the administration of loop drugs
options.C: Decreased blood volume can trigger orthostatic hypotension
options.D: Diuretics directly stimulate the heart to beat dangerously fast

explanation: Losing body fluid lowers blood volume, which can cause blood pressure to drop suddenly when the patient tries to stand up. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h7)

question: At what time of day should patients usually take their daily diuretic pill?
explanation: Taking the medication in the morning prevents frequent trips to the toilet at night and lets the patient sleep undisturbed. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h8)

question: Which foods are best to suggest for a patient taking a potassium-wasting diuretic?
explanation: Bananas and citrus fruits contain high amounts of potassium, which helps replace what is lost through loop or thiazide diuretics. [learn more](GNS223_U8_T1#GNS223_U8_T1_h8)
